frames.narration: Backtracking builds a solution one choice at a time: put a queen in this row, recurse to the next row, and when a branch is finished undo the choice and try the next column. With no checks until the board is full, 8 queens means every one of 8 to the power 8 boards: 19,173,961 nodes.

Prune. If two queens already attack each other, nothing placed in the remaining rows can repair it, so the whole subtree below is skipped. Checking each placement as it is made takes 8 queens from 19,173,961 nodes to 2,057, and it still finds the same 92 solutions.

Where you check matters. Only forbidding a reused column, and looking at the diagonals when the board is full, still visits 109,601 nodes: most of that work sits below placements that were already wrong. Check as early as a cheap, correct check allows.

Subset sum: count the subsets of 20 numbers that add up to half the total. Without pruning every item is in or out: 2,097,151 nodes. Prune when the running total passes the target, or when even all the remaining items cannot reach it: 726,739 nodes.

Order the items largest first. The total overshoots sooner, so the same two rules cut higher in the tree: 109,147 nodes for the same 6,722 matching subsets. An ordering heuristic does not change the answer, only how much of the tree is visited.

Order also decides how soon you find a first answer. For 24 queens, columns left to right need 411,609 nodes to reach one solution; the middle columns first need 65. To count every solution the order does not matter: 8 queens visit 2,057 nodes either way.

It is still exponential. Pruned 8, 9, 10 and 11 queens cost 2,057, 8,394, 35,539 and 166,926 nodes: four to five times more per queen. And for 20 equal items with a target just out of reach, the bounds rarely fire: 705,431 nodes against 2,097,151 unpruned.

So guard the search. Put a node or time budget on any solver that reads untrusted input, and when a small target makes the remaining-sum state repeat, switch to dynamic programming, which remembers sub-problems instead of re-walking them.
